summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) given right away with SABR given after a 3-month delay, in patients with metastatic lung, colorectal, or prostate cancer that has spread to 1 to 10 sites. Patients receive SABR immediately or after 3 months of standard of care, and the number of treatments is not stated. The study measures the impact of timing on survival.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara la radioterapia ablativa estereotáctica (SABR) administrada de inmediato con la SABR administrada después de un retraso de 3 meses, en pacientes con cáncer de pulmón, colorrectal o de próstata metastásico que se ha diseminado a 1 a 10 sitios. Los pacientes reciben la SABR de inmediato o después de 3 meses de tratamiento estándar, y el número de tratamientos no se indica. El estudio mide el efecto del momento del tratamiento en la supervivencia.
who_for: Age 1 year or older and willing to give informed consent
Histologically confirmed lung, prostate, or colorectal cancer with metastases seen on imaging
Newly diagnosed metastatic disease at 1 to 10 sites
not_for: No option for standard systemic therapy, or refuses systemic therapy
Chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 3 weeks before entry
Serious comorbidities that preclude radiotherapy, such as certain lung, bowel, or connective tissue conditions
Malignant pleural effusion or known brain metastases
